Story

📖

Hikoyani 3 marta o‘qing: avval jim, keyin audio bilan, keyin ovoz chiqarib.

A Sunday with my big family

🎧 Track 1.2 · StoryScan & listen

My name is Dilnoza and I live in Samarkand with my parents and my little brother. I’m not an only child, but sometimes I feel like one because my brother is ten years younger!

Every Sunday, all our relatives get together at my grandparents’ house. My grandma is very kind and calm. She looks after everyone and cooks a huge plov. My grandpa is a bit strict, but he is also really funny.

My aunt comes with her husband and their twins, Ali and Vali. They are my favourite cousins. I get on well with them because we grew up together. My uncle and his wife bring my niece, little Madina. Everyone says she looks like me!

My grandparents are very proud. They have five grandsons and three granddaughters. My parents got married twenty years ago, and they are still very close. My dad is a hard-working engineer.

I love Sundays because our family is loud, happy and full of love.

Answer the Questions

❓

Har bir savolga 2–3 gap bilan ovoz chiqarib javob bering.

  • 1How many people are there in your family?
  • 2Who do you look like in your family?
  • 3Who are you closest to? Why?
  • 4Do you get on well with your brothers and sisters?
  • 5Do you have a big or a small family?
  • 6How often do you see your relatives?
  • 7What do you do together at the weekend?

⭐ Answer + reason + example. Javob + sabab (because…) + misol (for example…).

Sample answers

💡 Who are you closest to? Why?

I’m closest to my mum. She’s very kind and she always listens to me. When I have a problem, I talk to her first.

💡 How often do you see your relatives?

Quite often! Every Sunday our relatives get together at my grandparents’ house. We eat plov and talk for hours.

Real Speaking

🎤

Bu sizning sahnangiz! Nutqni 4 xil qahramon bo‘lib ayting.

🎬 Model speech
🎧 Track 1.3 · SpeechScan & listen

Good morning! I’d like to tell you about my family. There are five of us: my parents, my two younger sisters and me. I’m the oldest. My dad works as an engineer and my mum is a teacher. Everyone says I look like my dad – we’re both tall and calm. I get on well with my sisters, but we sometimes argue about the TV! I’m closest to my mum because she’s so kind. At the weekend we usually visit our grandparents and all our relatives get together. Family is very important to me. Thank you!

Story

📖

Hikoyani 3 marta o‘qing: avval jim, keyin audio bilan, keyin ovoz chiqarib.

A day in Bobur’s life

🎧 Track 2.2 · StoryScan & listen

Bobur is a student in Tashkent, and he also works part-time in a café. His days are very busy!

He always wakes up at half past six, but he doesn’t get up immediately – he checks his phone first. Then he has a shower, gets dressed and has breakfast with his mum. He brushes his teeth and leaves home at half past seven to catch the bus.

His classes start at eight. At twelve he has lunch with his friends, and in the afternoon he goes to the café. He usually starts work at two and finishes work at six. He can take a break for fifteen minutes.

When he gets home, he often helps his mum. Sometimes he cooks dinner, and he does the housework twice a week. He hardly ever watches TV.

Bobur never goes to bed before midnight – he studies in the evening. He’s tired, but he loves his life!

🎬 Model speech
🎧 Track 2.3 · SpeechScan & listen

Hello everyone! Let me tell you about my daily routine. On weekdays I usually get up at seven o’clock. The first thing I do is drink a glass of water. After that, I have a shower, get dressed and have breakfast. It takes me about twenty minutes to get to school by bus. I have lunch at one and finish school at three. In the evening I like to play football or read. I hardly ever watch TV. At the weekend my routine is different – I get up late and visit my grandparents. Thank you!

Story

📖

Hikoyani 3 marta o‘qing: avval jim, keyin audio bilan, keyin ovoz chiqarib.

Three jobs, one family

🎧 Track 3.2 · StoryScan & listen

In the Karimov family, everyone has a different job.

The father, Rustam, is an engineer. He works in a big factory and he often works long hours. His salary is good, but he is always tired. He gets on very well with his colleagues.

His wife, Nilufar, is a nurse at a hospital. She works full-time and sometimes at night. She loves her job because she helps people.

Their son, Sardor, is a programmer. He works from home three days a week and goes to the office two days a week. His boss is young and friendly. Sardor earns money and also studies English in the evening.

Their daughter, Madina, is still a student, but she has a part-time job as a shop assistant. She is very good at talking to people. Her dream job is to be a doctor, and next month she has an important interview at a medical university.

Grandpa Hasan is retired now. He was a driver for forty years!

Hi everyone! Today I want to talk about my dream job. In the future I’d like to be a doctor. It isn’t an easy job – doctors work long hours and study for many years. But the best thing about this job is that you help people every day. My aunt works as a nurse in a hospital, and she tells me interesting stories. I’m good at biology and chemistry, and I’m not afraid of hard work. In my country, doctors get a good salary, but for me money isn’t the most important thing. I want a job I love. Thank you!

Story

📖

Hikoyani 3 marta o‘qing: avval jim, keyin audio bilan, keyin ovoz chiqarib.

Kamola’s new flat

🎧 Track 4.2 · StoryScan & listen

Last month, Kamola moved to a new flat in Tashkent. Before that, she lived in a big house with a garden in a village.

Her new flat is on the fifth floor of a modern building. It has two bedrooms, a living room, a small kitchen and a bathroom. Her favourite place is the balcony – she drinks her morning tea there. The flat isn’t very spacious, but it’s cosy. She doesn’t have much furniture yet – only a bed, a table and a big blue sofa.

Kamola likes her neighbourhood. There is a park opposite her building and a supermarket next to it. The metro is very near, so she isn’t far from her office.

There is one problem: the street is quite noisy in the evening, and the metro is always crowded. But her neighbours are very friendly – the old woman next door often brings her bread!

Kamola misses her quiet village a little, but she is happy in her new home.

Dilnoza’s birthday shopping

🎧 Track 5.2 · StoryScan & listen

Dilnoza’s birthday was on Saturday, and she wanted something new to wear. On Friday she went to a big shopping centre with her sister.

First, they looked at dresses. Dilnoza found a beautiful blue dress, but the price was very high – it was too expensive for her. Then they saw a sign: “Sale! 50% discount!”

She tried on three dresses. The first one didn’t fit – it was the wrong size. The second one was fashionable but not comfortable. The third one was perfect! She also bought a pair of white trainers and a warm scarf for her mum.

She wanted to pay by card, but the card machine wasn’t working, so she paid in cash.

On the way home they went to the market and bought fruit – it’s always cheap there. “I didn’t spend too much money,” Dilnoza said happily. Next time, maybe she will shop online!

Jasur’s new hobby

Jasur is sixteen. A year ago, he spent all his free time at home. He played computer games for hours, and his mum was not happy.

One day his uncle gave him an old camera. At first Jasur thought it was boring, but then he started to take photos of the city, people and animals. Now photography is his favourite hobby!

Last month he joined a photography club. They meet every Saturday and go for a walk in different parts of the city. Sometimes they visit a museum or a concert and take pictures there. Jasur says it’s really exciting.

He’s also interested in music. He’s learning to play the guitar, and he practises at least thirty minutes every day. He says it’s very relaxing.

At the weekend he meets friends, they go to the cinema or eat out. And computer games? He still plays sometimes, but he isn’t really into them any more.

Cooking plov with Grandma

🎧 Track 7.2 · StoryScan & listen

Every Sunday, Aziza cooks with her grandma. Last Sunday, Grandma said, “Today I’ll teach you my famous plov recipe!”

First, they bought the ingredients at the market: meat, rice, carrots, onions and some other vegetables.

At home, Aziza cut the onions and carrots – she cried a lot because of the onions! Grandma fried the meat in a big pot. Then they added the onions, the carrots and some salt. After that, they boiled some water and added the rice.

While the plov was cooking, Grandma baked fresh bread. The kitchen smelled wonderful, and Aziza was very hungry.

Finally, the plov was ready. The whole family said it was delicious – not too salty and not too spicy. For dessert they had fruit and some sweets with green tea.

Aziza’s brother usually eats junk food and orders pizza, but that day he said, “Plov is my favourite dish now!”

The most famous dish is plov. It’s made with rice, meat, carrots and onions. In my country, people usually eat plov for lunch, especially at weddings.

Story

Shahzod’s healthy year

🎧 Track 8.2 · StoryScan & listen

Last winter, Shahzod was often ill. He had a cold almost every month, he often had a headache, and once he had a temperature for three days. He took a lot of medicine. He decided to see a doctor. The doctor asked him some questions. “How much do you sleep? Do you do any sport?” Shahzod said, “I sleep five hours, and I’m a bit lazy – I never go to the gym.”

The doctor said, “You need to get enough sleep, drink more water and be more active.”

So Shahzod changed his life. Now he goes running three times a week and he goes swimming on Saturdays. He also joined a football team. Last week they played an important match, and they won!

He doesn’t eat much junk food now, and he lost five kilos of weight. He has less stress and he hardly ever feels sick. “I’m in really good shape now,” he says. “It’s easy to keep fit – you just need to start!”

Our first trip abroad

🎧 Track 9.2 · StoryScan & listen

Last summer, my family decided to go on holiday abroad for the first time. We chose Turkey! My mum booked a hotel online two months before, and Dad bought the tickets. The night before the trip, we packed our luggage – my sister wanted to take all her toys!

We went to the airport by car. Dad couldn’t find his passport for ten minutes – we were so nervous! We left at 6 a.m. and arrived in Istanbul at 9.

We stayed in Istanbul for three days. We went sightseeing and visited old mosques and markets. On the second day, we got lost in the small streets, but a kind man helped us.

Then we took a trip to Antalya by train and bus. We swam at the beach every day and explored the mountains near the town.

There were tourists from many countries.

Before we went home, I bought souvenirs for my friends. It was the best holiday ever!

Story

📖

Four seasons in Tashkent

🎧 Track 10.2 · StoryScan & listen

I’m Laylo from Tashkent. We have four very different seasons here. Summer is very hot – sometimes the temperature is 42 degrees! It’s sunny every day and it almost never rains. People stay indoors in the afternoon.

Autumn is my favourite season. It’s warm in September and cool in November. There are lots of fruits. Sometimes it’s cloudy and windy.

Winter can be cold, but it isn’t freezing every day. Sometimes it’s snowy. It gets dark very early – at five o’clock! In the mornings it’s often foggy.

In spring everything is green, and it’s often rainy, so I always take an umbrella. Sometimes there is a big storm. Before I leave home, I always check the weather forecast on my phone. I think our climate is great – you can enjoy every season!

Story

📖

Hikoyani 3 marta o‘qing: avval jim, keyin audio bilan, keyin ovoz chiqarib.

Grandpa’s photo album

🎧 Track 11.2 · StoryScan & listen

Last weekend, Grandpa showed me his old photo album. “Look, this is me,” he said. “I was born in a small village near Namangan in 1955. I grew up there. In my childhood we didn’t have a TV – we used to play outside all day.”

“Here I am as a teenager. I started school at seven, and I graduated from university in Tashkent. My parents were very proud.”

“We got married in 1980 and moved house to the city.”

Then he asked, “Have you ever flown on a plane?” “Yes, once,” I said. “But I was really scared!” Grandpa laughed. “I flew for the first time when I was forty. I was scared too!”

“Do you miss the village?” I asked. “Sometimes. I remember every street. I’ll never forget those days.”

It was an unforgettable afternoon. Then Grandpa asked, “Have you finished your homework yet?” I said, “I’ve just started!” I was a bit embarrassed.

Malika’s big plans

🎧 Track 12.2 · StoryScan & listen

Malika is seventeen, and she has a lot of plans for the future! First, she’s going to pass her IELTS exam in March. She works hard every day to improve her English. Her goal is band 7.

After that, she hopes to study abroad. She would like to study business in Malaysia or Korea. “It depends on the price,” she says. “I’m probably going to apply for a scholarship.”

She is also going to learn to drive this summer. Her dad promised to teach her.

In five years, she wants to come back to Uzbekistan and get a job in a big company. She plans to save money and buy a car.

But her biggest dream is to start her own business – a small café with books. “I don’t know when, but one day I’ll definitely do it,” she says. “I want to be successful and achieve my dreams!” Her parents decided to help her.
